caption: Have you ever noticed your baby clicking their tongue over and over again? 👀  It might seem like they're simply entertaining themselves, but they're actually practicing one of the most important muscle groups they'll use every day.  These little tongue movements help babies develop oral-motor coordination, the foundation for feeding, swallowing, and later, speech. Just like reaching for a toy or rolling over, babies learn through repetition. Every click is another opportunity to explore what their body can do.🙌  Give your child time, watch with curiosity, and let them experiment. Sometimes, development sounds exactly like this. Research shows that early tongue movements and oral exploration play an important role in developing oral-motor coordination and sensorimotor control during infancy. 🧠 Goldfield, E. C., et al. (2010). Premature Infant Swallowing: Patterns of Tongue-Soft Palate Coordination Based Upon Videofluoroscopy. Infant Behavior & Development.
